questions.question: Describe the mechanisms by which microbes from humans are dispersed into / the air.
questions.solution_html:
• Mechanisms of microbial dispersion into air (from humans)
  • • Sneezing and coughing release droplets. Talking and breathing produce aerosols. Shedding of
  • skin cells carrying microbes. Movement resuspends settled dust microbes. Poor ventilation
  • increases airborne spread.
questions.final_answer: increases airborne spread
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Apply the concept of phytovolatilization to remediate mercury-contaminated soil.
questions.solution_html:
• Phytovolatilization for mercury remediation
  • • Plants absorb mercury from soil - Convert to a less toxic volatile form - Release it into the
  • atmosphere through leaves - Reduce soil contamination - Eco-friendly and cost-effective method
questions.final_answer: atmosphere through leaves - Reduce soil contamination - Eco-friendly and cost-effective method
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain why Penicillium and Aspergillus fungi are considered good indicators of / indoor air quality and dampness problems.
questions.solution_html:
• Penicillium and Aspergillus as indoor air indicators
  • • Common fungi in indoor environments - Grow well in damp and humid conditions -Presence
  • indicates moisture problems - produce spores affecting air quality- Associated with allergies and
  • health issues
questions.final_answer: health issues
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain eutrophication.
questions.solution_html:
• Eutrophication
  • • Excess nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus) in water - Leads to algal bloom formation-Reduces
  • oxygen levels in water - Causes death of aquatic organisms - due to sewage and fertiliser runoff
questions.final_answer: oxygen levels in water - Causes death of aquatic organisms - due to sewage and fertiliser runoff

  • • Use biostimulation (adding nutrients) - Enhances growth of native oil-degrading microbes

questions.question: Discuss the concept of cometabolism in pesticide degradation.
questions.solution_html:
• Cometabolism in pesticide degradation ((10 marks))
  • • Definition: degradation of pesticide without being used as an energy source (2). Requires the
  • presence of another substrate (2) - Microbes produce enzymes for the primary substrate (2)
  • These enzymes act on the pesticide (2) - Leads to partial/complete breakdown of toxic
  • compounds (1) - Important in the removal of persistent pesticides from the environment (1)
questions.final_answer: compounds - Important in the removal of persistent pesticides from the environment
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a detailed note on water pollution and its sources.
questions.solution_html:
• Water pollution and its sources ((10 marks))
  • • Water pollution definition (2): Domestic sewage adds organic matter and microbes (2), Industrial
  • effluents release toxic chemicals/heavy metals (2), Agricultural runoff adds fertilisers and
  • pesticides (2). Other sources: oil spills, plastics, pathogens (1). Causes harm to aquatic life and
  • human health (1)
questions.final_answer: human health
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
